arcos-animas-quimixto.name: Arcos – Ánimas – Quimixto
arcos-animas-quimixto.short: Snorkelling at the pinnacles of Los Arcos, lunch at Las Ánimas and a stop in Quimixto. Departs 9:00 am from the Puerto Vallarta dock.
arcos-animas-quimixto.blurb: Eight hours that start with breakfast on board and end with salt on your skin. You swim among the pinnacles of Los Arcos, eat facing Las Ánimas and get off at Quimixto to walk to the waterfall. If it is your first time on the bay, this trip tells the whole story.
arcos-animas-quimixto.photoAlt: The pinnacles of Los Arcos seen from the sea

itinerary.title: Puerto Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and breakfast on board while the captain checks the sea report.

itinerary.title: We sail towards Los Arcos
itinerary.body: Half an hour hugging the south shore; the pinnacles appear in the distance.

itinerary.title: Snorkelling at Los Arcos
itinerary.body: An hour among the pinnacles and caves of the marine park, with the guide in the water.

itinerary.title: Lunch at Las Ánimas
itinerary.body: Grilled fish facing the beach and free time for kayaking or a hammock.

itinerary.title: Return from Quimixto
itinerary.body: A short walk to the waterfall and back to the dock with the sun low. Arrival around 5:30.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to swim?
faq.answer: No. The life jacket floats on its own and the guide stays with you in the water. Anyone who would rather not go in can watch Los Arcos from the deck.

faq.question: What if it rains?
faq.answer: With light rain we sail anyway; the bay is usually calm. If the harbour master closes the port, you change the date or we refund the deposit.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes, from 4 years old. We carry life jackets in every size and lunch at Las Ánimas gives them beach time.

faq.question: How much walking is there in Quimixto?
faq.answer: About 25 minutes along a trail to the waterfall. Anyone who would rather not walk stays on the beach or rides up on horseback at their own expense.

reviews.quote: The sea was calm and the snorkelling was incredible. We are coming back next month.

reviews.quote: Eight hours and not a minute of waiting. Lunch at Las Ánimas, feet in the sand, was the best part.

reviews.quote: The guide got in the water with the kids and taught them to use the snorkel. They came out beaming.

yelapa-majahuitas.name: Yelapa – Majahuitas
yelapa-majahuitas.short: A village with no road, a waterfall and the beach at Majahuitas. Snorkel gear, lunch and an open bar on board.
yelapa-majahuitas.blurb: Yelapa has no road: you arrive by sea and get around on foot. You climb to the waterfall, eat on the beach at Majahuitas and come back feeling you have been far away, even though you leave and return the same day.
yelapa-majahuitas.photoAlt: Boat off the beach at Yelapa

itinerary.title: Puerto Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and coffee. The captain explains the route and when we land on each beach.

itinerary.title: We sail south
itinerary.body: An hour along the coast; on the way you see Los Arcos and Las Ánimas from the boat.

itinerary.title: Yelapa and the waterfall
itinerary.body: A walk through the village up to the waterfall. A swim in the pool and a slice of banana pie on the way back.

itinerary.title: Lunch at Majahuitas
itinerary.body: A beach with no road and no signal. Lunch facing the sea and snorkelling from the shore.

itinerary.title: Return
itinerary.body: Back to the dock with the bar open. Arrival around 5:00.

faq.question: How far is the walk to the waterfall?
faq.answer: About 20 minutes through the village streets, with a gentle climb. Sandals work, but trainers are better.

faq.question: Is there phone signal at Majahuitas?
faq.answer: No. It is part of the charm: let people know before you leave that you will be offline until five.

faq.question: Can I pay in cash?
faq.answer: The deposit is by bank transfer or card; the balance is paid at the dock in cash or by card.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes, from 4 years old. The walk is easy and the beach at Majahuitas has no waves.

islas-marietas.name: Marietas Islands
islas-marietas.short: A biosphere reserve an hour from Nuevo Vallarta. Snorkelling at the Hidden Beach, bird watching and lunch on board. Groups of 12 at most.
islas-marietas.blurb: Twelve people, one guide and an island the reserve protects. You swim into the Hidden Beach, see birds that nest nowhere else in Mexico and eat on board while the boat rocks. Worth booking weeks ahead.
islas-marietas.photoAlt: The Hidden Beach seen from the sea

itinerary.title: Nuevo Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and breakfast on board. The guide hands out the reserve wristbands.

itinerary.title: We sail
itinerary.body: An hour towards open sea. In season we often cross paths with whales on the way.

itinerary.title: Hidden Beach
itinerary.body: You swim in through the tunnel with the guide, in the slot the reserve assigns us.

itinerary.title: Snorkelling and birds
itinerary.body: Snorkelling at Isla Redonda and a slow lap of Isla Larga to see the blue-footed booby.

itinerary.title: Return
itinerary.body: Lunch on board on the way back to Nuevo Vallarta. Arrival around 2:00.

faq.question: Is entry to the Hidden Beach guaranteed?
faq.answer: The reserve issues a limited number of wristbands per day and we hold them with your booking. If the sea does not allow entry, that day is swapped for snorkelling at Isla Redonda and we refund the difference.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to swim?
faq.answer: For the Hidden Beach, yes: you swim about 30 metres through a tunnel. Non-swimmers enjoy the rest of the trip from the boat.

faq.question: Why groups of 12?
faq.answer: It is the most the reserve allows per boat. That is why it pays to book weeks ahead.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes, from 6 years old and swimming well. Under-6s cannot enter the Hidden Beach under the reserve's rules.

reviews.quote: The captain took us to a cave where there was nobody else. The best day of the trip.

avistamiento-de-ballenas.name: Whale watching
avistamiento-de-ballenas.short: Season from December to March. A short trip with a certified guide and guaranteed sighting windows.
avistamiento-de-ballenas.blurb: Every winter the humpbacks come to Banderas Bay to give birth and raise their calves. We sail for four hours with a certified guide and a hydrophone on board to hear them sing. If we do not see them, you repeat the trip at no cost.
avistamiento-de-ballenas.photoAlt: Humpback whale breaching in Banderas Bay

itinerary.title: Nuevo Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and coffee. The captain explains the day's route from the sea report.

itinerary.title: We sail
itinerary.body: Forty minutes towards open sea. On the way we often cross paths with dolphins and rays.

itinerary.title: Sighting area
itinerary.body: Two hours off Punta Mita with the engine off. We lower the hydrophone to hear the song.

itinerary.title: Back along the bay
itinerary.body: We return hugging the coast. Arrival at the dock around 12:00.

includes: You repeat if we do not see them

faq.question: What if we do not see whales?
faq.answer: You repeat the trip at no cost on any day you like within the season. In ten years it has happened to us four times.

faq.question: Which departure is better, morning or afternoon?
faq.answer: The 8:00 am one has the flattest sea; the 3:00 pm one comes back with the sunset light. Whale activity is similar in both.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes. We carry life jackets in every size and the trip is short. For children under 4 we recommend the private boat.

faq.question: How close does the boat get?
faq.answer: Mexican regulations require 60 metres of distance and engines off. If they come closer on their own, we stay still.

reviews.quote: We left in the afternoon and came back with the sunset. The guide explained everything without turning it into a lecture.

reviews.quote: A mother with her calf thirty metres from the boat. Nobody spoke, only the hydrophone.
reviews.author: Sofía M.

reviews.quote: The first day they did not show up and we were allowed to repeat at no cost. The second day we saw four.
reviews.author: Karla and Beto

charter-privado.name: Private charter
charter-privado.short: The whole boat for your group: route, schedule and menu your way. Weddings, birthdays and company outings.
charter-privado.blurb: The whole boat, the route you want and the schedule that suits you. We bring the crew, the music, the bar and the food; you decide where to anchor, how long to stay and when to head back.
charter-privado.photoAlt: Private boat sailing across the bay
charter-privado.itineraryTitle: A typical day, to give you an idea

itinerary.title: The dock, at your time
itinerary.body: Departures from 8:00 am. The boat is waiting with the music and the bar ready.

itinerary.title: First stop
itinerary.body: Snorkelling at Los Arcos or Las Caletas, depending on the route we have put together.

itinerary.title: Lunch on board
itinerary.body: A menu your way: ceviche, grilled fish or whatever the group asks for, in advance.

itinerary.title: Beach and sunset
itinerary.body: We anchor at Las Ánimas or Majahuitas for kayaking, paddle boarding and a swim to the shore.

itinerary.title: Return
itinerary.body: Back to the dock with the sunset or, if the group prefers, at night with the lights of the boardwalk.

faq.question: How many people fit on the boat?
faq.answer: Up to 16 people comfortably. For bigger groups we sail with two boats side by side.

faq.question: How is it priced?
faq.answer: By sailing hours and number of people. Tell us the date, the group and the idea of the route and we quote on WhatsApp the same day.

faq.question: Can we bring our own food and drinks?
faq.answer: Yes, at no charge. If you prefer, we put the menu and the bar together for you in advance.

faq.question: Do you do weddings and events?
faq.answer: Yes. Weddings, birthdays, bachelor parties and company outings. We can arrange decoration, cake and a photographer with local suppliers.
